instructions: Complete each sentence with the correct ending from the list. There are two more endings than you need.

items.prompt: Dr Elena Marsh argued that ring patterns are most dependable as...
items.answer: a calendar for fixing the dates of human activity
options: a guide to past summer temperatures when density is also measured
a calendar for fixing the dates of human activity
the chemical composition of the wood itself
combining ring evidence with other independent records
the absence of clear annual rings in many species
a direct measure of rainfall anywhere in the world
counting rings alone without comparing different samples

evidence.quote: ring patterns are most dependable as a calendar, a way of fixing the dates of buildings, ships and other human activity

items.how: Find the first researcher named in the paragraph on disagreement. Match the stem's phrase most dependable to the claim she makes, then compare it with the endings.
items.again: Test the temperature ending against her warning in the same sentence. Two endings concern climate, and she rejects the idea of reading temperatures directly, so read her full position.

items.prompt: Professor Samuel Ferreira claimed that, at cold northern sites, ring width and density can serve as...
items.answer: a guide to past summer temperatures when density is also measured
options: a guide to past summer temperatures when density is also measured
a calendar for fixing the dates of human activity
the chemical composition of the wood itself
combining ring evidence with other independent records
the absence of clear annual rings in many species
a direct measure of rainfall anywhere in the world
counting rings alone without comparing different samples

evidence.quote: the width and density of the late-summer band together provide a reliable guide to past summers

items.how: Locate Ferreira in the same paragraph and read what he says about cold sites. Note which two features of the ring he combines, then look for the matching ending.
items.again: Check that the ending mentions density, as he does. A different ending talks about rainfall in general, which the passage never links to his argument and which no researcher claims.

items.answer: the chemical composition of the wood itself

evidence.quote: the next major advance will come from analysing the chemical composition of the wood

items.how: Find Nwosu's position and underline what she says the next advance will come from. The ending must name the thing analysed rather than a method of counting.
items.again: Compare it with the ending about counting rings alone. That ending sounds technical, yet nothing in her argument supports it, and it describes a practice the writer treats as too simple.

evidence.quote: many species grow throughout the year and so lack clear annual rings altogether

items.how: Search the passage for the tropics rather than for a named researcher. Read the whole sentence, because the reason is given after the word since.
items.again: Check that your ending refers to the rings themselves. Another ending mentions rainfall, but the writer ties the difficulty to one biological feature of tropical species.

evidence.quote: the strongest results come from combining ring evidence with other independent records

items.how: Go to the closing paragraph and find the sentence that begins with for that reason. Match its main clause to one of the endings.
items.again: Notice that the ending must describe combining sources, not relying on one. The researchers in the previous paragraph each favour a single approach, which is why none of their views fits here.
